text:
alex: Heads up — gpu-az2-12 (r12-u04) is showing repeated Xid 13s and rising ECC corrected counts since last night. Before we return it to service I want a formal soak/burn-in to try to reproduce. Node: gpu-az2-12, card index: 1 (A100-40G).

marta: Can you paste the dmesg snippet and the `nvidia-smi -q` ECC section?

alex: dmesg snippet: 
```
[Apr 9 03:12:14] NVRM: Xid (13): 0: 31728 0x8080b89e 0x00000000
[Apr 9 03:25:40] NVRM: Xid (13): 0: 31728 0x80c0a1b3 0x00000000
[Apr 9 04:02:08] NVRM: Xid (13): 0: 31728 0x80d0f44f 0x00000000
```
`nvidia-smi -q` ECC: "Single-bit ECC errors": 128 (was 120 yesterday). Temps steady 42C. No OOMs logged.

vik: My proposal: run a 72h soak combo: 48h gpu-burn (SM stress) + 24h memtestG80 on the card, then a 24h production inference replay (seq=2048) to catch decoding-related hangs. If any Xid or ECC increments happen during the soak -> escalate replacement. If stable, return with a 48h canary.

samir: Minimal step list I use:
1) Drain node from k8s (kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets).
2) Cold power-cycle and reseat GPU.
3) Run `memtestG80 -t 24h` per card.
4) Run `gpu-burn` or `gpu-burn64` for 48h at full SM util.
5) Replay production trace `replay-infer --profile seq=2048 --duration 24h`.
6) Poll `dmesg` and `nvidia-smi -q` every 4h and upload logs.
If anything reproduces, collect logs and open vendor RMA.

alex: Quick automation snippet (will expand in infra repo):
```
#!/bin/bash
NODE=gpu-az2-12
ssh $NODE "sudo systemctl stop kubelet && sudo kubectl drain $NODE --ignore-daemonsets"
sleep 30
# power-cycle step done manually
./memtestG80 -d /dev/nvidia1 -t 24h || exit 2
./gpu-burn -d /dev/nvidia1 -T 48h || echo "gpu-burn failure" >> /tmp/soak_fail
# start replay
replay-infer --node $NODE --seq 2048 --duration 24h || echo "replay fail" >> /tmp/soak_fail
# collect counters
nvidia-smi -q > /tmp/nvidia-q.txt
sudo dmesg | tail -n 200 > /tmp/dmesg-tail.txt
aws s3 cp /tmp s3://redwood-gpu-logs/gpu-az2-12/1751009876/ --recursive
```

oncall-bot: :warning: Draining gpu-az2-12 will reduce available GPUs in az2 from 19 -> 18. Confirm?

marta: Confirmed, proceed. Also add a mandatory cold reboot + reseat before memtest — sometimes riser contacts cause intermittent ECCs.

vik: Note: if Xid appears only under PCIe stress tests, suspect riser/cable/slot — try swapping to spare riser before RMA. Also check BIOS/PCIe firmware and NVML versions; older firmware can trigger weird Xid under heavy loads. Record firmware versions in the automation report.

samir: I'll run the job and pipe logs to S3 at `s3://redwood-gpu-logs/gpu-az2-12/1751009876/`. I'll also setup a simple watcher to post when ECC counters increase or when Xid lines appear. Will tag this job `soak-1751009876`.

alex: Plan on marking the node `regen-soak:in-progress`. If it passes all stages with zero new Xids and ECC delta <= 2, we tag `regen-soak:passed` and return to rotation behind a 48h canary. If failure, escalate to vendor RMA with attached memtest/gpu-burn logs.

oncall-bot: Scheduled soak start: 2025-04-10T02:30:00Z end target: 2025-04-13T02:30:00Z. Notifications to #eng-infra and oncall. Job id: soak-1751009876.

marta: Ops/finance note — pulling a spare card from the pool for replacement is ~$4k immediate cost. Prefer to confirm fail from soak before pulling RMA.

vik: Also include NVLink stress if node uses NVLink. And be sure to check `dmesg` for other PCIe errors (AER) or thermal throttles. If intermittent Xid only during memory tests, swap riser and re-run to isolate.

alex: Starting drain now. Will post first logs after reseat + memtest kickoff. :thumbsup:
